plan: This is a second-price auction, where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding above my value adds risk of overpaying (paying more than my value), while bidding below reduces my chances of winning profitably. Bidding exactly my value of $10 ensures I win whenever it's profitable to do so, and never pay more than my value. This maximizes expected profit given the auction mechanics.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In second-price auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth if others bid high; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $30, I will bid exactly $30 to ensure optimal outcomes in this single-round game.
